root_cause.text: rxrpc's `rxgk_verify_response()` created an `rxgk` context object but failed to release it on its return/error paths, causing a reference leak in the rxgk security handling code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both failure branches from `goto out;` to `goto out_gk;` and adds `rxgk_put(gk);` before the existing `key_put(key);`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state “Fix leak of rxgk context in rxgk_verify_response()” and “clean up the rxgk context it creates.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: rxrpc's `rxgk_verify_response()` created an `rxgk` context object but failed to release it on its return/error paths, causing a reference leak in the rxgk security handling code.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes both failure branches from `goto out;` to `goto out_gk;` and adds `rxgk_put(gk);` before the existing `key_put(key);`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state “Fix leak of rxgk context in rxgk_verify_response()” and “clean up the rxgk context it creates.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure `rxgk_verify_response()` always drops the `gk` reference before exit to fix a resource leak on success and error paths.
intent_record.what: The error-path gotos after `rxrpc_abort_conn()` and `rxgk_verify_authenticator()` were changed from `goto out;` to `goto out_gk;`, and a new `out_gk:` label was added before `out:` to call `rxgk_put(gk);` prior to `key_put(key);` and returning.
intent_record.how: This makes the function release the `gk` reference on both failure paths and also on the normal success path before exiting, preventing a leaked `gk` reference that would otherwise persist when control jumped directly to `out`.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure `rxgk_verify_response()` always drops the `gk` reference before exit to fix a resource leak on success and error paths.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the stated root cause by ensuring rxgk_verify_response() releases the gk context reference on all exit paths, preventing the reference leak.

candidates.rationale: This error-path exit transfers control to the common return path that only releases `key` and not the created `gk` context, directly causing the reference leak described in the root cause.
This second early-exit path also reaches the shared cleanup label without dropping the `gk` reference, so the created rxgk context leaks on authentication verification failure.
The common cleanup label is the defective exit point because it performs only `key_put(key);` and returns, omitting the required release of the `gk` object on both success and error paths.
The cleanup path releases only `key`; the absence of a corresponding `gk` release here is the direct cleanup bug that leaves the rxgk context referenced.
The success path falls through to the same incomplete cleanup sequence, so after successful verification the function still exits without dropping the created `gk` reference.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the incomplete common cleanup in rxgk_verify_response(). It releases only key and omits releasing the created gk context, which is the direct cause of the reference leak on both success and error exits.
This common exit label routes returns through a cleanup path that does not drop the gk reference, making it the defective exit point for the leaked context.
These early exits transfer control to the incomplete out cleanup path, causing the created gk context to leak when verification exits on error.
The success path sets a successful return value and then falls through to the same incomplete cleanup path, so the gk reference is still leaked on successful verification.

Author: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>

    rxrpc: rxgk: Implement the yfs-rxgk security class (GSSAPI)
    
    Implement the basic parts of the yfs-rxgk security class (security index 6)
    to support GSSAPI-negotiated security.
    
    Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
    cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
    cc: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it fully shows creation and all visible return/error paths for the rxgk context object in `rxgk_verify_response()`. The vulnerable construct is present: `gk = rxgk_generate_transport_key(conn, token->rxgk, sp->hdr.cksum, GFP_NOFS);` creates/acquires an `rxgk_context`, but there is no matching `rxgk_put(gk)` anywhere in the function. After successful creation, the code uses `krb5 = gk->krb5;`, then on decrypt failure does `goto out;`, on authenticator verify failure does `goto out;`, and even on success does `goto out;` after `conn->key = key; key = NULL; ret = 0;`. The `out:` label only does `key_put(key);` and returns, so the `gk` reference is leaked on both success and error paths after creation. Therefore the function contains the bug, and the fix is not present because no cleanup of `gk` was added on return/error paths.
